summary: The application attracted one of the largest public responses recorded on Falkirk Council's portal: about 6,700 objections against 80 messages of support by the 2 July 2026 consultation close, rising to more than 7,100 comments in late-July reporting. An APRS coalition letter published on 23 August recorded 7,020 objections uploaded to the portal as at 22 August; the figures may reflect different cut-offs or categories. Organised opposition includes Say No To Larbert Data Centre, The Inches and Kinnaird Village Residents Association and Larbert Residents Association, alongside APRS and Stop Climate Chaos Scotland. A Change.org petition was recorded at 5,402 signatures on 22 August and displayed 5,884 when checked on 3 September. More than 100 people attended a protest on 13 August, while APRS described the attendance as hundreds. Police Scotland's consultation response anticipated substantial public opposition and recommended robust site security. Apatura and Scottish Enterprise present the scheme as major inward investment with jobs and green-design commitments.

principal_concerns.concern: Proximity to sensitive uses — objectors state the site is close to housing, a nursery and Forth Valley Royal Hospital, and reportedly only ~20 m from a care home
Air quality and noise from 200 emergency backup diesel generators (campaigners compare emissions to '106,000 idling diesel cars' during testing)
principal_concerns.developer_response: Apatura states generators are for emergency backup only with periodic testing, and that the campus is designed to green-charter standards.

principal_concerns.concern: Scale of electricity demand (300MW; combined with Auchtertool, Fife, 900MW — just under a quarter of Scottish peak demand) and possible impact on energy prices

Adequacy of consultation and of environmental information; complexity of a 52-document environmental submission; APRS argues the proposal is contrary to the development plan and calls for a moratorium on hyperscale AI data centres
Water use and pressure concerns (drawing on reported experience near US data centres)
principal_concerns.developer_response: Apatura states a closed-loop cooling system will minimise water use.

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: More than 5,000 construction jobs a year and 1,300+ long-term operational jobs (500+ local at ~£56,000 average salary)
'District heat ready' design offering potential future heat supply to local homes/businesses; no off-taker, network or funding identified
Almost £1bn of direct investment in Scotland

stakeholder_positions.position: Formal objection: contrary to development plan, inadequate environmental information; seeks refusal and a national moratorium on hyperscale AI data centres.

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: Say No To Larbert Data Centre
stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed; organised objection drives, a public meeting on 25 June 2026 and the 13 August protest.

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: The Inches and Kinnaird Village Residents Association
stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed; signed the community-campaign coalition letter calling for a moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions pending national safeguards.
Opposed; signed the community-campaign coalition letter calling for a moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions pending national safeguards.
Supportive as landowner/economic agency: 'Scotland welcomes the ambition and scale' (Victoria Carmichael).

Its consultation response anticipated 'a great deal of public opposition' and recommended robust security against protest-related disruption or vandalism. This was operational advice rather than an objection on the planning merits.

notes: All objection, comment and petition totals are point-in-time figures. The 7,020 figure is APRS's count of objections uploaded to the portal as at 22 August 2026; earlier press described more than 7,100 comments in late July, so the categories may not be like-for-like. Change.org totals are self-reported and volatile: 5,402 signatures were recorded in the coalition letter as at 22 August and 5,884 were displayed when the petition was checked on 3 September. The council reportedly continues to accept late representations. A pre-determination hearing is reportedly required before decision.
